Synopsis:
The U.S. trade deficit widened sharply to $88.6bn in July, driven by record capital goods imports ($140.3bn) tied to AI infrastructure buildout. Exports fell 2.1%, partly on lower crude oil and gold shipments. Record bilateral goods deficits were posted with Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, South Korea and Malaysia despite aggressive tariffs, signaling tariff policy is failing to compress import demand. Trade is set to be a drag on Q3 GDP, echoing the -1.14pp subtraction in Q2.
